transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

A drop in drying performance plus a smell usually points to a build-up of lint (fluff), so cleaning is a good first step. First, though, work out what kind of smell it is:

• Burning, hot or electrical smell: Stop using the dry function and unplug the machine. Lint near the heater can scorch and is a fire risk, and it can also mean a failing heating element. Do the checks below, and if the smell continues, call an engineer.
• Musty, damp or "eggy" smell: This is usually mould or bacteria in the seal, drawer or drain filter. It's unpleasant but not dangerous.

## Things to clean

1. Drain pump filter (most important)
On most Hotpoint washer dryers this sits behind a small flap at the bottom front.
• Put down towels and a shallow tray, as water will come out.
• Unscrew the filter slowly, let it drain, then pull it out.
• Clear out fluff, coins, hair grips and other debris, and rinse it.
• Screw it back in firmly.

In drying mode, the machine condenses moisture into water that has to drain away. If this filter is clogged, the machine can't remove the moisture, so clothes stay damp. Gunk trapped here is also a common source of smells.

2. Door seal
Pull back the rubber folds and wipe out fluff, hair and any black mould. Diluted washing-up liquid or a mild bleach solution works well, but rinse afterwards.

3. Detergent drawer
Pull it out fully (there's usually a release tab) and scrub it. Also check the cavity it slides into, where mould often hides.

4. Maintenance wash
Run an empty hot wash (90°C, or the "drum clean" program if yours has one) with a washing machine cleaner or soda crystals. This removes detergent and fabric conditioner residue that traps lint inside the machine.

## Other common causes

• Overloading: Washer dryers can only dry about half their wash capacity. For example, a 9kg washer dryer typically dries around 6kg. Overloaded loads come out damp.
• Low spin speed: Wetter clothes going into the dry cycle take much longer to dry.
• Water supply: Many washer dryers use cold water to condense the steam. Check the tap is fully on and the inlet hose isn't kinked.
• Lint build-up in the condenser: This is the internal duct the machine uses to remove moisture, and lint inside it can block it. It's usually self-cleaning, but if the steps above don't help, it may need professional attention.

Tip: running regular hot washes and not overdoing fabric softener helps stop lint and residue building up again.

If you tell me your model number (on a sticker inside the door or on the back), I can try to give more specific guidance.

It's more of a burning dust, scorched fabric kind of smell, not musty. The top of the machine gets very hot too, and I think I saw a faint haze by the door seal once. I've still been using it though. The model is NDB 9635 W UK.

Please stop using the machine now and unplug it. A scorched smell, a very hot top and a visible haze (likely smoke) together point to something overheating inside, which is a genuine fire risk. Washer dryer fires often start this way.

## What to do now

1. Unplug it at the wall. Don't just switch it off at the button.
2. Don't use it at all until it's been checked, including wash-only cycles. The dry function is the main concern, but it's safest to rule out an electrical fault first.
3. Don't take it apart or clean inside it yourself. The fluff that causes this builds up in the internal drying duct, condenser and around the heater, which can only be reached by removing panels near mains wiring. Cleaning the drain filter or door seal won't fix it.
4. Make sure you have a working smoke alarm nearby.

## Why this is more than a cleaning job

The likely causes include:
• Heavy lint build-up in the drying duct or around the heater, which can scorch or ignite
• A failed thermostat or thermal cut-out. These should shut the heater off before it gets dangerously hot, so a very hot top and a scorched smell suggest one may not be working.
• A failing fan, which stops hot air moving so heat builds up
• A faulty heating element or wiring

An engineer needs to diagnose which it is.

## Getting it looked at

• Contact Hotpoint's service team through hotpoint.co.uk. Describe exactly what you told me: the burning smell, the hot top and the haze. This tells them it's a safety issue, not just poor drying.
• Check for any recall. Hotpoint has had safety recalls on some machines in the past. Enter your model and serial number (on the sticker inside the door rim) into Hotpoint/Whirlpool's online recall checker, and look at the UK government's product safety alerts at gov.uk. I'm not aware of a recall on your model, but it's worth checking because a recall repair would be free.
• If it's still under warranty or you have appliance cover, the repair may be free anyway.

If you ever see actual smoke or flames, unplug it only if it's safe to do so, get everyone out, and call 999.
